task_summary: Implement a PID temperature controller: calibrate HVAC system, identify parameters, tune controller gains, run closed-loop control to 22.0C, and compute performance metrics.
decomposition_rationale: The task has four sequential phases (calibration, system identification, controller tuning, closed-loop control+metrics) but they share tight coupling through the simulator and PID logic. Decomposing into two skills: (1) system identification from step-response data, and (2) PID controller with tuning and metrics computation, provides clean separation of concerns while avoiding over-decomposition.

skills.name: evo-thermal-sysid
skills.description: System identification utilities for first-order thermal systems. Runs open-loop step tests on the HVAC simulator, collects calibration data, fits first-order exponential model using scipy.optimize.curve_fit, and outputs estimated parameters (K, tau) with fit quality metrics.
skills.responsibility: Open-loop calibration data collection, noise filtering (Savitzky-Golay), first-order step response curve fitting, parameter estimation (K, tau), R-squared calculation, and JSON serialization of calibration_log.json and estimated_params.json.
dr_sections: 1. First-Order Thermal System Identification from Step Response Data
1.4 Handling Sensor Noise and Filtering Data
1.5 Evaluating Fit Quality: R-Squared and Errors

skills.name: evo-thermal-pid-control
skills.description: PID controller tuning, discrete-time PID implementation with anti-windup, closed-loop simulation execution, and control performance metrics computation. Takes estimated system parameters, computes SIMC gains, runs the controller against the HVAC simulator, and evaluates rise time, overshoot, settling time, and steady-state error.
skills.responsibility: SIMC/IMC gain calculation (Kp, Ki, Kd), discrete-time PID controller with trapezoidal integration and anti-windup clamping, closed-loop simulation loop management, performance metrics calculation (rise_time, overshoot, settling_time, steady_state_error, max_temp), and JSON serialization of tuned_gains.json, control_log.json, and metrics.json.
dr_sections: 2. PID Controller Tuning from Identified First-Order Model Parameters
2.1 IMC (Internal Model Control) and Lambda Tuning
7.4 Off-by-One Errors in Settling Time Calculation
